testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To keep cargo in a large box.
To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
To prevent cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding when the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from the body?

options.text: Faster if the person stays awake.

questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a steady rate. Coffee, cold showers, and other tricks do not speed this up. Only time will make you sober.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To prevent cargo from being loaded too high.
To prevent cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What can rough acceleration cause?

options.text: It helps you stay awake on long trips.

questions.explanation: Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle. Always accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: What is a thin layer of ice on the road called?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks wet. Be careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: How should cargo in a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no higher than three feet.
It should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo in a trailer must be properly secured to prevent it from moving during transport.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you start driving. If you have a trailer, it must be straight for mirrors to be checked correctly.

questions.question: What must you be to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Able to do your own background check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. You will lose it if you give up your U.S. citizenship.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: The state will notify your employer.
Tell your employer within two business days.
Tell your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you are disqualified from driving.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not miss checking something important.

questions.question: How does a truck's weight affect stopping distance?

options.text: It usually has no impact on stopping distance
It is a major factor affecting stopping distance
It is not as important as the type of cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major factor affecting stopping distance
questions.explanation: A truck's weight is important for stopping distance. Heavier trucks need more braking power to stop completely.

questions.question: If other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane on a multilane road if your truck is moving slowly. This allows other vehicles to pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who does not know the rules of the road

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are on drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign of impairment is stopping at inappropriate places, like green traffic lights.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually have:
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks usually have high centers of gravity. Be careful when driving with them because the contents can shift while the truck is moving.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Allowed if you contact your employer

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and is never permitted when operating a truck.

questions.question: How often should you use your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Only when there may be a problem

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around your vehicle at all times. Make it a habit to check your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: The liver can process about ____ per hour.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the higher your blood alcohol will become. Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent an engine fire from spreading?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to help stop an engine fire from spreading.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on every wheel of a truck. The most common type of foundation brake is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put a balanced amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how the weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put a balanced amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be balanced properly. Too much weight over an axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight over an axle can reduce traction and make the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should inspect the windshield. Which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your windshield, look for cracks or damage that could affect your view of the road. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and loose attachment.

questions.question: When you pull over on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should be your main way to control speed?
questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use your engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Slow down and downshift before you start going down the hill. If you rely too much on the brakes, they can overheat and stop working well.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice an unusual noise or feeling, what should you do?

options.text: Hope the vehicle makes it until another driver takes over.
Stop and investigate to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and investigate to find the problem.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what you see, hear, smell, and feel while driving. This helps you spot mechanical problems early. If you notice anything unusual, stop and check it out.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo.

questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: While driving, which statement about texting is true?

options.text: You cannot send a text, but you can read one.
You can send a text, but you cannot read one.
You cannot send or read a text.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot send or read a text.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is not allowed. Texting includes typing text on a device or reading text on a device.

questions.question: Before a pre-trip inspection, you should look under the vehicle to check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is on an incline.
Fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel.
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel.
questions.explanation: Before inspection, check the vehicle's overall condition and make sure it is not damaged or tilted. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Show other drivers that you are angry.
Warn other drivers that you are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Your horn warns others of your presence. Because the horn can startle drivers and create danger, use it only when necessary.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, how should you start?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, start by turning the steering wheel opposite to the direction you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts means the nuts are loose. Check how tight they are before you drive.

questions.question: ABS allows you to:
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) helps stop your wheels from locking up when you brake hard. Drive and brake the same way whether you have ABS or not.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Notify emergency services of your problem and your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are exiting the bus.
Is a concern whether or not passengers are visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern whether or not passengers are visible.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around stopped buses. Passengers may be getting on or off, and the bus may block your view of them or their view of you.

questions.question: If an applicant does not receive an air brakes endorsement:

options.text: They cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes.
They can only operate a vehicle with air brakes in intrastate commerce.
They can only operate a vehicle with air brakes in interstate commerce.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes test and use a vehicle with air brakes to pass your skills test to be licensed to drive a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer:

options.text: The trailer doors should be opened.
The trailer doors should not be opened.
A large, heavy blanket should be put over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer doors should not be opened.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes it bigger and more dangerous.

questions.question: As part of a pre-trip inspection, you should look for all of the following, except:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: Check your tires for proper air pressure, wear, and cracks. Make sure front tires have at least 4/32 inch tread depth and other tires have at least 2/32 inch tread depth. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when beginning to move forward from a stopped position, you should:
questions.explanation: For a manual transmission vehicle, partly engage the clutch before you release the brake pedal to prevent rolling backward.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts means the nuts are loose. Check how tight they are before you drive.

questions.question: How do ice cream trucks become hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must be kept cold.
Children often run toward an ice cream truck without looking for other traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave trails of water and ice on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward an ice cream truck without looking for other traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children. Children often do not look for traffic when they run to or from ice cream trucks.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: In cold weather, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the roadway.
Before other parts of the roadway.
At the same time as other parts of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the roadway.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Drive carefully on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: On the front, rear, and sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo. They must be visible from all directions.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: How should you hold warning triangles when placing them on the road?

options.text: Hold them between yourself and oncoming traffic.
Carry them behind your back so other drivers don't see you until they are placed.
Hold them as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold them between yourself and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Tie-downs secure cargo on flatbed trailers and closed vans to keep it from shifting or falling off while moving. Shifting cargo can affect how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a construction worker near the road?
questions.explanation: Always slow down in work zones. Reduce your speed when workers are on or near the roadway.

questions.question: How much water is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A large amount, like a puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on the road and slide on a thin layer of water. Even a small amount of water can cause this.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The state will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must inform your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also inform your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state.

questions.question: How often should you stop to take a break while driving?
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, stop for a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles.
